title.zh: 卷322 列傳一百九 窦光鼐 李漱芳 范宜宾 曹锡宝 谢振定 钱沣 尹壮图
title.en: Volume 322 Biographies 109: Dou Guangnai, Li Shufang, Fan Yibin, Cao Xibao, Xie Zhending, Qian Feng, Yin Zhuangtu
title.raw: 卷322 列傳一百九 窦光鼐 李漱芳 范宜宾 曹锡宝 谢振定 钱沣 尹壮图

sentences.zh: =竇光鼐=竇光鼐，字元調，山東諸城人。

translations.literal: Dou Guangnai, courtesy name Yuandiao, was a man of Zhucheng in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Guangnai, styled Yuandiao, came from Zhucheng in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 乾隆七年進士，選庶吉士，散館授編修。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Qianlong he became a jinshi, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and upon leaving the academy was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in 1742, entered the Hanlin Academy as a probationer academician, and on completing his term was made a compiler.

sentences.zh: 大考四等，罰俸。

translations.literal: In the grand examination he received the fourth grade and was fined salary.
translations.idiomatic: He scored fourth class in the palace examination and was fined a portion of his salary.

sentences.zh: 高宗夙知光鼐，居數月，擢左中允。

translations.literal: The Gaozong Emperor had long known Guangnai; within several months he was promoted to Left Vice Director of Studies.
translations.idiomatic: The Qianlong Emperor had known him for some time; a few months later he was promoted to Left Vice Director of Studies.

sentences.zh: 累遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand Secretary of the Imperial Cabinet.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to Grand Secretary of the Imperial Cabinet.

sentences.zh: 二十年，授左副都御史。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was appointed Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In 1755 he was appointed Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 督浙江學政。

translations.literal: He supervised education in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He served as educational commissioner for Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 上南巡，臨海縣訓導章知鄴將獻詩，光鼐以詩拙阻之。

translations.literal: When the Emperor made a southern tour, Zhang Zhiye, instructor of Linhai County, was about to present a poem; Guangnai blocked him because the poem was crude.
translations.idiomatic: During an imperial southern tour, Zhang Zhiye, an instructor from Linhai County, prepared to present a poem, but Guangnai stopped him because the verse was poor.

sentences.zh: 知鄴欲訐光鼐，光鼐以聞。

translations.literal: Zhiye wished to impeach Guangnai; Guangnai reported this to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiye tried to denounce Guangnai; Guangnai reported the matter to the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 上召知鄴試以詩，詩甚拙，且言原從軍。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned Zhiye to test him with poetry; the poem was very crude, and he also said he had originally been in the military.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor summoned Zhiye for a poetic trial; his poem was wretched, and he admitted he had once been a soldier.

sentences.zh: 上斥其妄，命奪職戍闢展。

translations.literal: The Emperor rebuked his presumption and ordered his dismissal and exile to guard Bizhan.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor denounced his effrontery, stripped him of his post, and sentenced him to banishment at Bizhan.

sentences.zh: 後數年，上欲赦知鄴還，而知鄴妄為悖逆語，欲以陷光鼐，上乃誅之。

translations.literal: Several years later the Emperor wished to pardon Zhiye and recall him, but Zhiye spoke rebellious words in presumption, intending to entrap Guangnai, whereupon the Emperor had him executed.
translations.idiomatic: Years later the Emperor meant to pardon and recall him, but Zhiye uttered seditious words meant to frame Guangnai, and the Emperor had him put to death instead.

sentences.zh: 光鼐學政任滿，還京師。

translations.literal: When Guangnai's term as educational commissioner ended, he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When his tenure as educational commissioner ended, he returned to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 秋讞，光鼐以廣西囚陳父悔守田禾殺賊，不宜入情實；

translations.literal: In the autumn assize, Guangnai held that Chen Fuhui, a Guangxi prisoner who had killed a thief while guarding his crop in the field, should not be entered as intentional murder;
translations.idiomatic: At the autumn assizes, Guangnai argued that Chen Fuhui, a Guangxi convict who killed a thief while defending his crops, should not be classified as intentional murder;

sentences.zh: 貴州囚羅阿扛逞兇殺人，不宜入緩決：持異議，簽商刑部，語忿激。

translations.literal: that Luo Akang, a Guizhou prisoner who had murdered in violent arrogance, should not enter deferred execution: he maintained dissenting views, countersigned for consultation with the Ministry of Punishments, and his words were furious.
translations.idiomatic: and that Luo Akang, a Guizhou murderer who had killed in violent arrogance, should not be entered for reprieve. He lodged objections and signed the file for discussion with the Ministry of Punishments, speaking with heated indignation.

sentences.zh: 刑部遽以聞，上命大學士來保、史貽直，協辦大學士梁詩正覆覈，請如刑部議，且言光鼐先已畫題，何得又請改擬。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Punishments hurriedly reported to the throne; the Emperor ordered Grand Secretaries Laibao and Shi Yizhi, together with Associate Grand Secretary Liang Shizheng, to review again, requesting accordance with the ministry's proposal, and stating that Guangnai had already signed the memorial—how could he again request revision.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Punishments reported the matter at once. The Emperor ordered Grand Secretaries Laibao and Shi Yizhi, with Associate Grand Secretary Liang Shizheng, to re-examine the cases. They recommended following the ministry's decision and noted that Guangnai had already signed the memorial—why was he asking now to revise the draft?

sentences.zh: 上詰光鼐，光鼐言：「兩案異議，本屬簽商，並非固執。

translations.literal: The Emperor questioned Guangnai; Guangnai said: "In both cases the dissent was originally for countersigned consultation, not obstinate insistence.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor interrogated Guangnai, who replied: "My objections in both cases were meant for countersigned consultation, not stubborn insistence.

sentences.zh: 因會議時言詞過激，刑部遽將簽出未定之稿先行密奏。

translations.literal: Because my words were too heated in conference, the Ministry of Punishments hastily submitted the unsigned draft in secret memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Because I spoke too sharply in conference, the Ministry of Punishments submitted the unsigned draft to Your Majesty in a secret memorial before consultation was finished.

sentences.zh: 臣未能降心抑氣，與刑部婉言，咎實難辭，請交部嚴加議處。

translations.literal: Your servant failed to lower his heart and restrain his spirit, to speak gently with the Ministry of Punishments—the fault is truly hard to escape, and I beg to be handed over to the ministry for severe disciplinary deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: I failed to check my temper and negotiate courteously with the ministry. The fault is plainly mine; I beg that my case be referred to the ministry for strict discipline."

sentences.zh: 」上以「會讞大典，光鼐意氣自用，甚至紛呶謾罵而不自知。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "At the great assize assembly, Guangnai is self-willed in spirit, even shouting abuse and not knowing it himself.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "At a formal judicial conference Guangnai indulges his temper to the point of shouting abuse without even noticing it.

sentences.zh: 設將來預議者尤而效之，於國憲朝章不可為訓」。

translations.literal: If in future those participating in deliberation take this as an example to emulate, it cannot serve as instruction for national statutes and court regulations."
translations.idiomatic: If future participants take this as precedent, it will undermine the authority of law and court discipline—this cannot be tolerated."

sentences.zh: 命下部嚴議，當左遷，仍命留任。

translations.literal: He ordered the ministry to deliberate strictly; demotion was appropriate, but he still ordered him to remain in office.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the ministry to deliberate strict punishment, which warranted demotion, but still directed that Guangnai keep his post.

sentences.zh: 光鼐疏言：「事主殺竊盜，律止杖徒。

translations.literal: Guangnai memorialized: "When the householder kills a thief, the statute only prescribes beating or penal servitude.
translations.idiomatic: Guangnai memorialized: "When a homeowner kills a burglar, the code provides only beating or imprisonment.

sentences.zh: 近來各省多以竊盜拒捕而被殺，比罪人不拒捕而擅殺，皆以鬥論，寬竊盜而嚴事主，非禁暴之意。

translations.literal: In recent years many provinces treat the killing of a thief who resisted arrest as fighting, comparing it to the criminal who kills without resistance—lenient to thieves and strict to householders, which is not the intent of checking violence.
translations.idiomatic: Yet lately many provinces classify such killings as fighting, treating them like unpremeditated homicide during brawling—indulgent toward thieves and harsh toward householders, which defeats the purpose of restraining lawlessness.

sentences.zh: 應請遵本律。

translations.literal: [We] should request to follow the original statute.
translations.idiomatic: The original statute should be applied."

sentences.zh: 」議行。

translations.literal: The proposal was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The recommendation was approved and implemented.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，上以光鼐迂拙，不勝副都御史，命署內閣學士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, the Emperor considered Guangnai pedantic and clumsy, unfit for Vice Censor-in-Chief, and ordered him to serve as acting Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In 1762 the Emperor judged Guangnai too rigid and tactless for a vice censor-in-chief post and reassigned him as acting grand secretary of the cabinet.

sentences.zh: 授順天府府尹。

translations.literal: He was appointed Prefect of Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed prefect of Shuntian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 坐屬縣蝗不以時捕，左遷四品京堂，仍留任。

translations.literal: Because subordinate counties did not catch locusts in season, he was demoted to a fourth-rank capital office but retained in post.
translations.idiomatic: When subordinate counties failed to control locusts on schedule, he was demoted to a fourth-rank capital post but allowed to remain in office.

sentences.zh: 旋赴三河、懷柔督捕蝗，疏言：「近京州縣多旗地，嗣後捕蝗，民為旗地佃，當一體撥夫應用。

translations.literal: Soon he went to Sanhe and Huairou to supervise locust-catching, memorializing: "Near the capital many counties have banner lands; henceforth in catching locusts, when commoners are tenants on banner land, laborers should be assigned uniformly.
translations.idiomatic: He soon went to Sanhe and Huairou to supervise locust control and reported: "Because many counties near the capital include banner estates, tenants farming banner land should be mustered for locust duty on equal terms with other farmers.

sentences.zh: 」上從所請，以諭直隸總督楊廷璋。

translations.literal: The Emperor acceded to the request and transmitted instructions to Zhili Governor Yang Tingzhang.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved and relayed the order to Zhili Governor Yang Tingzhang.

sentences.zh: 廷璋言自方觀承始設護田夫，旗、民均役。

translations.literal: Tingzhang said that since Fang Guancheng had instituted field-guard laborers, bannermen and commoners shared equal service.
translations.idiomatic: Yang replied that field-guard laborers had been instituted under Fang Guancheng, with bannermen and civilians serving alike.

sentences.zh: 上復以詰光鼐，召還京師，令從軍機大臣入見。

translations.literal: The Emperor again questioned Guangnai, recalled him to the capital, and ordered him to appear with the Grand Council members.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor questioned Guangnai again, summoned him back to Beijing, and required him to audience alongside the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 問：「民為旗地佃，不肯撥夫應用，屬何人莊業？

translations.literal: He asked: "When commoners as tenants on banner land refuse to supply laborers, whose estate management is this?
translations.idiomatic: He asked whose estate managers were responsible when tenant farmers on banner land refused to supply laborers.

sentences.zh: 」光鼐不能對，請徵東北二路同知及三河、順義知縣質證。

translations.literal: Guangnai could not answer and requested to summon the subprefects of the two northeast circuits and the magistrates of Sanhe and Shunyi for testimony.
translations.idiomatic: Guangnai could not answer and asked that the subprefects of the northeast circuits and the magistrates of Sanhe and Shunyi be summoned to testify.

sentences.zh: 退又疏請罷護田夫，別定派夫捕蝗事例。

translations.literal: After retiring he again memorialized to abolish field-guard laborers and separately fix regulations for assigning labor for locust-catching.
translations.idiomatic: On withdrawing he memorialized again to abolish field-guard laborers and establish separate rules for locust labor levies.

sentences.zh: 上以光鼐所見迂鄙紕繆，下部議，奪職。

translations.literal: The Emperor deemed Guangnai's views pedantic, vulgar, and erroneous; handed to the ministry for deliberation and stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor found his proposals pedantic and mistaken, referred him to the ministries for judgment, and stripped him of his post.

sentences.zh: 居數月，諭光鼐但拘鈍無能，無大過，左授通政司副使。

translations.literal: After several months, the edict stated Guangnai was merely obtuse and incompetent without major fault, and he was demoted-left to Vice Commissioner of the Court of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: Months later the Emperor ruled that Guangnai was merely dull and inept rather than guilty of grave misconduct, and demoted him to vice commissioner of the Court of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 再遷宗人府府丞。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred again, to vice director of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 复督浙江學政，擢吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Again he supervised Zhejiang education and was promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was reappointed educational commissioner for Zhejiang and promoted to vice minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 浙江州縣倉庫多虧缺，上命察覈。

translations.literal: In Zhejiang many prefectural and county granaries showed deficits; the Emperor ordered inspection.
translations.idiomatic: Many Zhejiang prefectural and county granaries showed shortfalls; the Emperor ordered an audit.

sentences.zh: 光鼐疏言：「前總督陳輝祖、巡撫王亶望貪墨敗露，總督富勒渾未嚴察。

translations.literal: Guangnai memorialized: "Former Governor Chen Huizu and Governor-General Wang Danwang's corruption was exposed, yet Governor-General Fulehun did not investigate strictly.
translations.idiomatic: Guangnai reported: "After Governors Chen Huizu and Wang Danwang were exposed for corruption, Governor-General Fulehun failed to investigate rigorously.

sentences.zh: 臣聞嘉興、海鹽、平陽諸縣虧數皆逾十萬，當察覈分別定擬。

translations.literal: Your servant hears that in Jiaxing, Haiyan, Pingyang and other counties the deficits all exceed one hundred thousand; they should be inspected and separately determined.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that shortfalls in Jiaxing, Haiyan, Pingyang, and other counties each exceed one hundred thousand taels; they should be audited and penalties set case by case."

sentences.zh: 」上嘉其持正，命尚書曹文埴、侍郎姜晟往會巡撫伊齡阿及光鼐察覈。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised his uprightness and ordered Ministers Cao Wenchi and Vice Minister Jiang Sheng to go and join Governor-General Yiling'a and Guangnai in inspection.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor commended his integrity and sent Ministers Cao Wenchi and Jiang Sheng to join Governor-General Yiling'a and Guangnai in conducting the audit.

sentences.zh: 旋疏劾永嘉知縣席世維借諸生穀輸倉；

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized to impeach Xi Shiwei, magistrate of Yongjia, for borrowing grain from licentiates to fill the granary;
translations.idiomatic: He soon impeached Xi Shiwei, magistrate of Yongjia, for borrowing grain from licentiates to fill the granary;

sentences.zh: 平陽知縣黃梅假彌虧苛斂，且於母死日演劇；

translations.literal: Huang Mei, magistrate of Pingyang, for falsely concealing deficits and levying harsh exactions, and for staging opera on the day his mother died;
translations.idiomatic: Huang Mei, magistrate of Pingyang, for concealing deficits, extorting levies, and staging an opera on the day his mother died;

sentences.zh: 仙居知縣徐延翰斃臨海諸生馬寘於獄；

translations.literal: Xu Yanhan, magistrate of Xianju, for beating to death the licentiate Ma Zhi of Linhai in prison;
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yanhan, magistrate of Xianju, for beating to death the licentiate Ma Zhi of Linhai in prison;

sentences.zh: 並及布政使盛住上年詣京師，攜貲過豐，召物議；

translations.literal: and also the Provincial Administration Commissioner Sheng Zhu, who when going to the capital the previous year carried excessive wealth, arousing public criticism;
translations.idiomatic: and Provincial Administration Commissioner Sheng Zhu, whose unusually large baggage on his trip to the capital the year before had drawn public suspicion;

sentences.zh: 總督富勒渾經嘉興，供應浩煩，餽閽役數至千百。

translations.literal: Governor-General Fulehun, passing through Jiaxing, had supplies so lavish that gifts to gate servants reached hundreds and thousands.
translations.idiomatic: and Governor-General Fulehun, whose passage through Jiaxing had involved lavish hospitality and gifts to gate servants numbering in the hundreds and thousands.

sentences.zh: 上命大學士阿桂如浙江按治。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Grand Secretary Agui to go to Zhejiang to investigate and punish.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Grand Secretary Agui to Zhejiang to investigate and adjudicate.

sentences.zh: 阿桂疏言盛住詣京師，附攜應解參價銀三萬九千馀，非私貲；

translations.literal: Agui memorialized that when Sheng Zhu went to the capital he carried along silver of thirty-nine thousand-odd taels due for ginseng tribute, not private goods;
translations.idiomatic: Agui reported that Sheng Zhu had carried thirty-nine thousand-odd taels of silver due for ginseng tribute payment, not private goods;

sentences.zh: 平陽知縣黃梅母九十生日演劇，即以其夕死；

translations.literal: Pingyang Magistrate Huang Mei's mother had opera on her ninetieth birthday and died that very evening;
translations.idiomatic: that Huang Mei's mother had turned ninety on the day of the opera and died that same evening;

sentences.zh: 仙居諸生馬寘誣寺僧博，復與鬥毆，因下獄死。

translations.literal: Xianju licentiate Ma Zhi falsely accused a temple monk of gambling, then fought with him and died in prison as a result.
translations.idiomatic: and that Ma Zhi had falsely accused a temple monk of gambling, fought with him, and died in prison after being detained.

sentences.zh: 光鼐語皆不仇。

translations.literal: Guangnai's statements did not match.
translations.idiomatic: None of Guangnai's charges matched the facts.

sentences.zh: 光鼐再疏論梅事，言阿桂遣屬吏詣平陽諮訪，未得實，躬赴平陽覆察。

translations.literal: Guangnai again memorialized on Mei's case, saying Agui sent subordinate officials to Pingyang to inquire but did not obtain the facts, and he personally went to Pingyang to re-investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Guangnai memorialized again on Huang Mei's case, saying Agui's subordinates had inquired in Pingyang without establishing the facts, so he went there himself to reinvestigate.

sentences.zh: 伊齡阿再疏劾光鼐赴平陽刑迫求佐證諸狀，上責光鼐乖張瞀亂，命奪職，逮下刑部。

translations.literal: Yiling'a again memorialized to impeach Guangnai for going to Pingyang and using torture to coerce corroborating testimony; the Emperor rebuked Guangnai as perverse and confused, ordered dismissal, and handed him to the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Yiling'a impeached him again, charging that in Pingyang he had used torture to extract corroborating testimony. The Emperor denounced Guangnai as reckless and muddled, stripped him of office, and handed him over to the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 光鼐尋奏：「親赴平陽，士民呈梅派捐單票，田一畝捐大錢五十；

translations.literal: Guangnai soon memorialized: "I personally went to Pingyang; gentry and commoners presented Mei's levy receipts—fifty large cash per mu of field;
translations.idiomatic: Guangnai soon submitted: "When I went to Pingyang in person, local gentry and commoners presented Huang Mei's levy receipts, charging fifty large cash per mu;

sentences.zh: 又勒捐富戶數至千百貫；

translations.literal: he also compelled donations from wealthy households reaching hundreds and thousands of strings;
translations.idiomatic: he also extorted donations from wealthy households amounting to hundreds and thousands of strings;

sentences.zh: 每歲採買倉穀不予值。

translations.literal: each year in purchasing granary grain he did not pay the price.
translations.idiomatic: each year he purchased granary grain without paying fair value.

sentences.zh: 梅在縣八年，所侵穀值及捐錢不下二十萬。

translations.literal: Mei was in the county eight years; the grain value he embezzled and donations did not fall short of two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In eight years as magistrate, the grain he misappropriated and the levies he extorted totaled no less than two hundred thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 母死不欲發喪，特令演劇。

translations.literal: When his mother died he did not wish to hold mourning and specially ordered opera performed.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he delayed the funeral and staged the opera instead.

sentences.zh: 」上以光鼐呈單票有據，時阿桂已​​還京師，令復如浙江秉公按治，並命江蘇巡撫閔鶚元會讞，以光鼐質證。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Guangnai's presented receipts had evidence, and Agui had already returned to the capital, ordered him again to go to Zhejiang to investigate impartially, and also ordered Jiangsu Governor Min E'yuan to join in assize, using Guangnai to testify.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor found Guangnai's receipts convincing. Agui had already returned to Beijing, so the Emperor sent Guangnai back to Zhejiang to investigate impartially and ordered Jiangsu Governor Min E'yuan to join the assize and take Guangnai's testimony.

sentences.zh: 阿桂、鶚元疏言梅婪索事實，論如律。

translations.literal: Agui and E'yuan memorialized that Mei's extortion was factual and sentenced according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Agui and Min reported that Huang Mei's extortion was established and sentenced him according to law.

sentences.zh: 上以光鼐所奏非妄，命署光祿寺卿，阿桂、文埴、晟、伊齡阿皆下部議。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Guangnai's memorial was not false, ordered him to serve as acting Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; Agui, Wenchi, Sheng, and Yiling'a were all handed to the ministry for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ruled that Guangnai's charges were not false and appointed him acting minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, while Agui, Cao Wenchi, Jiang Sheng, and Yiling'a were all referred to the ministries for disciplinary review.

sentences.zh: 旋擢光鼐宗人府府丞。

translations.literal: Soon Guangnai was promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: Guangnai was soon promoted to vice director of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 复督浙江學政。

translations.literal: Again he supervised Zhejiang education.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed educational commissioner for Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 再遷左都御史。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again, to Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 六十年，充會試正考官，榜發，首歸安王以铻，次王以銜，兄弟聯名高第。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year he served as chief examiner of the metropolitan examination; when the list was published, first was Wang Yiyue of Gui'an, second Wang Yixian—brothers ranking high together.
translations.idiomatic: In 1795 he served as chief metropolitan examiner. When the results were published, Wang Yiyue of Gui'an ranked first and Wang Yixian second—brothers who had placed at the top together.

sentences.zh: 大學士和珅素嫉光鼐，言於上，謂光鼐迭為浙江學政，事有私。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Heshen had long resented Guangnai; he spoke to the Emperor, saying Guangnai had repeatedly been Zhejiang educational commissioner and the matter had private interest.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Heshen, who had long resented Guangnai, told the Emperor that because Guangnai had repeatedly served as Zhejiang educational commissioner, the affair involved favoritism.

sentences.zh: 上命解任聽部議，及廷試，和珅為讀卷官，以銜復以第一人及第，事乃解。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered removal from office pending ministry deliberation; at the palace examination Heshen was reader of papers, and Yixian again placed first—then the matter was resolved.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Guangnai dismissed pending ministry review. At the palace examination Heshen served as reader of papers, and Yixian again placed first, after which the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 命予四品銜休致。

translations.literal: He was ordered granted fourth-rank insignia and retirement.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted fourth-rank insignia and retired.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: =李漱芳=李漱芳，字藝圃，四川渠縣人。

translations.literal: Li Shufang, courtesy name Yipu, was a man of Qu County in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shufang, styled Yipu, came from Qu County in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十二年進士，授吏部主事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Qianlong he became a jinshi and was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in 1757 and was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 再遷郎中。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again, to director.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，授河南道監察御史。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he was appointed Censor of the Henan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1768 he was appointed censor of the Henan circuit.

sentences.zh: 巡視中城，尚書福隆安家奴藍大恃勢縱恣，挾無賴酗酒，橫行市肆間。

translations.literal: Inspecting the central city, Minister Fulong'an's bondservant Lan Da relied on power and acted wantonly, taking with ruffians to drink wine and rampage through market streets.
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting the central city, he found Lan Da, a bondservant of Minister Fulong'an, abusing his master's power, drinking with ruffians, and terrorizing the markets.

sentences.zh: 漱芳捕治，論奏，高宗深嘉之，命戍藍大，以福隆安下吏議。

translations.literal: Shufang arrested and punished him, memorialized for judgment; the Gaozong Emperor deeply praised this, ordered Lan Da exiled, and handed Fulong'an to officials for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Shufang arrested and prosecuted him. The Qianlong Emperor greatly commended the action, sentenced Lan Da to banishment, and referred Fulong'an to the ministries for review.

sentences.zh: 尋擢工科給事中。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Supervising Secretary of the Board of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to supervising secretary of the Board of Works.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，壽張民王倫為亂。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year the Shouzhang commoner Wang Lun raised rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In 1774 the Shouzhang commoner Wang Lun led a rebellion.

sentences.zh: 漱芳疏陳奸民聚眾滋事，為飢寒所迫；

translations.literal: Shufang memorialized that wicked commoners gathered crowds to make trouble, compelled by hunger and cold;
translations.idiomatic: Shufang reported that the rebels had gathered because they were driven by hunger and cold;

sentences.zh: 又言近畿亦有流民扶老攜幼，遷徙逃亡，有司監盧溝橋，阻不使北行。

translations.literal: he also said that near the capital there were also refugees supporting the old and carrying the young, migrating in flight, and officials guarded Lugou Bridge and blocked them from going north.
translations.idiomatic: and that refugees near the capital were fleeing with the elderly and children while officials at Lugou Bridge were blocking them from traveling north.

sentences.zh: 給事中範宜賓亦以為言，請增設粥廠。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Fan Yibin also spoke similarly, requesting additional gruel kitchens.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Fan Yibin made similar claims and asked that additional soup kitchens be established.

sentences.zh: 上命侍郎高樸、袁守侗率宜賓、漱芳往盧溝橋及近畿諸城鎮省視，初無流民。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Vice Ministers Gao Pu and Yuan Shoutong to lead Yibin and Shufang to inspect Lugou Bridge and nearby capital towns and markets; initially there were no refugees.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Vice Ministers Gao Pu and Yuan Shoutong, with Fan and Shufang, to inspect Lugou Bridge and nearby towns. They found no refugees at first.

sentences.zh: 倫亂定，俘其徒檻致京師廷鞫，命漱芳旁視，無言為飢寒迫者。

translations.literal: When Lun's rebellion was settled, his followers were captured in cangues and brought to the capital for court interrogation; the Emperor ordered Shufang to observe at the side—none spoke of being compelled by hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was suppressed, captives were brought to Beijing in cangues for trial. Shufang was ordered to observe. None claimed they had been driven by hunger or cold.

sentences.zh: 問歲事，對秋收尚及半。

translations.literal: Asked about the year's harvest, they answered the autumn harvest was still more than half.
translations.idiomatic: Asked about the harvest, they replied that more than half the autumn crop remained.

sentences.zh: 上責漱芳妄言，代奸民解說，心術不可問，不宜复居言路，為世道人心害，宥罪，降禮部主事。

translations.literal: The Emperor rebuked Shufang for false speech, speaking on behalf of wicked commoners; his mind could not be questioned—he should not again occupy the remonstrance path, harming worldly principle and human hearts; his crime was pardoned and he was demoted to Principal Clerk in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor rebuked Shufang for fabricating reports and excusing rebels. His motives were suspect; he should not hold a remonstrance post again lest he harm public morals. His life was spared, but he was demoted to principal clerk in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，禮部請以漱芳升授員外郎。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year the Ministry of Rites requested Shufang be promoted to Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In 1778 the Ministry of Rites nominated Shufang for promotion to vice director.

sentences.zh: 故事，郎中、員外郎員缺，選應升授者，擬正、陪上請。

translations.literal: By precedent, when Director and Vice Director posts were vacant, those selected for promotion were nominated as principal and alternate for imperial request.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, when director and vice director posts fell vacant, candidates for promotion were nominated in principal and alternate pairs for imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 至是，獨以漱芳請。

translations.literal: At this time, only Shufang was nominated.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion, however, only Shufang was nominated.

sentences.zh: 上不懌，責尚書永貴擅專邀譽，涉明季黨援朋比之習，奪其職。

translations.literal: The Emperor was displeased, rebuked Minister Yonggui for acting on his own to seek praise, touching the Ming-season habit of factional patronage and cliquishness, and stripped him of office.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was displeased and rebuked Minister Yonggui for seeking credit on his own, accusing him of reviving late-Ming habits of factional patronage. Yonggui was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 漱芳久之乃遷員外郎。

translations.literal: Only after a long time was Shufang transferred to Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Only much later was Shufang promoted to vice director.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: =範宜賓=範宜賓，漢軍鑲黃旗人，大學士文程後也。

translations.literal: Fan Yibin, a Han Bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner, was a descendant of Grand Secretary Wencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yibin, a Han bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner, was a descendant of Grand Secretary Wencheng.

sentences.zh: 以廕生官戶部郎中，歷御史給事中，累遷太常寺少卿。

translations.literal: By yinsheng he became a Director in the Ministry of Revenue, passed through censor and supervising secretary posts, and was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Entering office by inheritance privilege, he became a director in the Ministry of Revenue, served as censor and supervising secretary, and rose to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 出為安徽布政使，與巡撫胡文伯不相能，兩江總督高晉以聞。

translations.literal: He went out as Anhui Provincial Administration Commissioner, could not get along with Governor Hu Wenbo, and Liangjiang Governor-General Gao Jin reported this.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as Anhui provincial administration commissioner but clashed with Governor Hu Wenbo, prompting Liangjiang Governor-General Gao Jin to report the conflict.

sentences.zh: 上召宜賓還，授左副都御史。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned Yibin back and appointed him Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor recalled Fan and appointed him Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 宜賓奏言屬縣蝗見，屢請捕治，文伯執不可。

translations.literal: Yibin memorialized that locusts appeared in subordinate counties; he repeatedly requested catching and control, but Wenbo insisted it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Fan reported locust infestations in subordinate counties and repeatedly urged control measures, but Hu Wenbo refused.

sentences.zh: 上為黜文伯，而宜賓亦以捕蝗不力下吏議，當左遷。

translations.literal: The Emperor dismissed Wenbo for this, but Yibin also was handed to officials for deliberation for ineffective locust-catching, warranting demotion.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor dismissed Hu Wenbo, but Fan was also referred to the ministries for failing to control the locusts effectively and was slated for demotion.

sentences.zh: 上以宜賓舊為御史尚黽勉，命仍為御史。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Yibin had formerly been a censor and still strove diligently, ordered him to remain a censor.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Fan had once served as a censor and still showed diligence, the Emperor kept him in that post.

sentences.zh: 宜賓疏言籓臬有所陳奏，輒呈稿督撫，當禁飭。

translations.literal: Yibin memorialized that when provincial and circuit officials had matters to memorialize, they always presented drafts first to governors and governors-general, which should be forbidden and admonished.
translations.idiomatic: Fan memorialized that provincial and circuit officials habitually submitted draft memorials to their governors first and urged that the practice be forbidden.

sentences.zh: 上以整飭吏治，要在朝廷綱紀肅清，自無扶同蒙蔽之事，不在設法峻防，置其議不行。

translations.literal: The Emperor said that to rectify official governance, what mattered was that court discipline be clear and strict; there would naturally be no covering up and concealment, and there was no need to devise harsh preventive measures—his proposal was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor replied that sound governance depended on clear court discipline, not on suspicion and harsh preventive rules, and rejected the proposal.

sentences.zh: 及與漱芳同被譴，上以宜賓漢軍世僕，乃敢妄言幹譽，特重其罰，奪職，戍新疆。

translations.literal: When he was condemned together with Shufang, the Emperor said that Yibin, as a hereditary Han banner bondservant, yet dared speak falsely to seek praise, and especially increased his punishment: dismissal and exile to Xinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: When he was punished along with Shufang, the Emperor held that as a hereditary Han banner bondservant Fan had dared speak falsely for credit and imposed a heavier sentence: dismissal and banishment to Xinjiang.

sentences.zh: =曹錫寶=曹錫寶，字鴻書，一字劍亭，江南上海人。

translations.literal: Cao Xibao, courtesy name Hongshu and also Jianting, was a man of Shanghai in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xibao, styled Hongshu and also known as Jianting, came from Shanghai in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，以舉人考授內閣中書，充軍機處章京。

translations.literal: Early in Qianlong, by examination as a provincial graduate he was appointed Secretariat Drafter of the Imperial Cabinet and served as a clerk of the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianlong reign he qualified through examination as a provincial graduate, became a secretariat drafter, and served as a Grand Council clerk.

sentences.zh: 資深當擢侍讀，錫寶辭。

translations.literal: When seniority warranted promotion to Reader, Xibao declined.
translations.idiomatic: When seniority made him eligible for promotion to reader, Xibao declined.

sentences.zh: 大學士傅恆知其欲以甲科進，乃不為請遷。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Fu Heng knew he wished to advance through the top examination degree and therefore did not request his transfer.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Fu Heng knew he hoped to advance through the palace examination and did not recommend him for promotion.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，成進士，改庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he became a jinshi and was made a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1757 he passed the jinshi examination and entered the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 以母憂歸，病瘍，數年乃愈。

translations.literal: He returned home for his mother's mourning, fell ill with ulcers, and only recovered after several years.
translations.idiomatic: He went home to mourn his mother, fell ill with ulcers, and took several years to recover.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，散館，改刑部主事。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he left the Hanlin Academy and was transferred to Principal Clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In 1766 he completed his Hanlin term and was appointed principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 再遷郎中。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again, to director.

sentences.zh: 授山東糧道。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grain Intendant of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed grain intendant of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 衛千總寧廷言子惠以索逋殺千總張繼渠，錫寶下部議。

translations.literal: Guard company commander Ning Tingyan's son Hui killed company commander Zhang Jiqu while collecting a debt; Xibao referred the case to the ministry for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: When guard company commander Ning Tingyan's son Hui killed fellow commander Zhang Jiqu while collecting a debt, Xibao referred the case to the ministries for judgment.

sentences.zh: 上巡山東，召見，命來京以部屬用。

translations.literal: When the Emperor toured Shandong, he summoned him for audience and ordered him to come to the capital for use as a ministry subordinate.
translations.idiomatic: During an imperial tour of Shandong he was summoned for audience and ordered to the capital for appointment within the ministries.

sentences.zh: 以大學士阿桂奏，令入四庫全書館自效。

translations.literal: On Grand Secretary Agui's memorial, he was ordered to enter the Siku Quanshu project to prove himself.
translations.idiomatic: On Grand Secretary Agui's recommendation he was assigned to the Siku Quanshu compilation project.

sentences.zh: 書成，以國子監司業升用。

translations.literal: When the books were completed, he was promoted for service as Vice Director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: When the compilation was finished he was promoted to vice director of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 居三年，上以錫寶補司業無期，特授陝西道監察御史。

translations.literal: After three years, the Emperor, because Xibao's appointment as Vice Director had no fixed date, specially appointed him Censor of the Shaanxi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After three years, with no timely vacancy for the vice directorship, the Emperor specially appointed him censor of the Shaanxi circuit.

sentences.zh: 時協辦大學士和珅執政，其奴劉全恃勢營私，衣服、車馬、居室皆踰制。

translations.literal: At the time Associate Grand Secretary Heshen held power; his bondservant Liu Quan relied on influence to seek private gain, and his clothing, carriages, horses, and residence all exceeded regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Associate Grand Secretary Heshen was then in power. His bondservant Liu Quan abused that influence for private gain, with clothing, carriages, and residence all exceeding prescribed limits.

sentences.zh: 錫寶將論劾，侍郎南匯吳省欽與錫寶同鄉里，聞其事，和珅方從上熱河行在，馳以告和珅，令全毀其室，衣服、車馬有踰制，皆匿無跡。

translations.literal: Xibao was about to memorialize for impeachment; Vice Minister Wu Shengqin of Nanhui, a fellow townsman of Xibao, heard of the matter; Heshen was then with the Emperor at the Rehe traveling palace—he hurried to inform Heshen, who ordered Quan to destroy his house; clothing, carriages, and horses that exceeded regulations were all hidden without trace.
translations.idiomatic: Xibao prepared to impeach him. Vice Minister Wu Shengqin of Nanhui, a fellow townsman, learned of it and, with Heshen accompanying the Emperor at Rehe, rushed word to him. Heshen ordered Liu Quan to demolish his house and hide every item of clothing, carriage, or horse that exceeded regulations.

sentences.zh: 錫寶疏至，上詰和珅。

translations.literal: When Xibao's memorial arrived, the Emperor questioned Heshen.
translations.idiomatic: When Xibao's memorial arrived, the Emperor interrogated Heshen.

sentences.zh: 和珅言平時戒約嚴，或扈從日久漸生事，乞嚴察重懲。

translations.literal: Heshen said he was strict in admonition in normal times, but perhaps from long attendance on tour misconduct had gradually arisen, and begged strict investigation and heavy punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Heshen said he normally kept strict discipline but that long service on tour may have bred misconduct, and begged for a strict investigation and severe punishment.

sentences.zh: 乃命留京辦事王大臣召錫寶問狀，又令步軍統領遣官從錫寶至全家察視，無跡，錫寶自承冒昧。

translations.literal: He then ordered the prince-minister handling affairs in the capital to summon Xibao to question the case, and also ordered the Metropolitan Infantry Commandant to send officials with Xibao to inspect Quan's entire household—no trace was found, and Xibao himself admitted rashness.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered the prince-minister in Beijing to summon Xibao for questioning and sent officials from the Metropolitan Infantry Command with him to search Liu Quan's household. They found nothing, and Xibao admitted he had acted rashly.

sentences.zh: 上召錫寶詣行在面詰，錫寶奏全倚勢營私，未有實跡，第為和珅「杜漸防微」，乃有此奏。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned Xibao to the traveling palace for face-to-face questioning; Xibao memorialized that Quan relied on power to seek private gain, though there was no concrete evidence, and only to "check the first sprout and guard against the slight" for Heshen did he make this memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor summoned Xibao to the traveling palace and questioned him in person. Xibao said Liu Quan had abused power for private gain but that he lacked concrete proof and had memorialized only to "nip evil in the bud" on Heshen's behalf.

sentences.zh: 复諭軍機大臣、大學士梁國治等覆詢，錫寶又承「杜漸防微」語失當，請治罪。

translations.literal: Again he ordered Grand Council members and Grand Secretary Liang Guozhi and others to question further; Xibao again admitted the phrase "check the first sprout and guard against the slight" was improper and requested punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor again ordered the Grand Council and Grand Secretary Liang Guozhi to question him further. Xibao again admitted the "nip evil in the bud" wording was improper and asked to be punished.

sentences.zh: 下部議，當左遷。

translations.literal: The case was handed to the ministry for deliberation; demotion was appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries deliberated and recommended demotion.

sentences.zh: 上手詔略言：「平時用人行政，不肯存逆詐億不信之見。

translations.literal: The Emperor personally issued an edict in brief saying: "In normal times in employing men and administering affairs, I am unwilling to harbor a view of anticipating deceit and presuming disbelief.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor personally issued an edict stating: "In appointing officials and governing affairs I refuse to begin from suspicion and distrust.

sentences.zh: 若委用臣工不能推誠佈公，而猜疑防範，據一時無根之談，遽入人以罪，使天下重足而立、側目而視，斷無此政體。

translations.literal: If in entrusting ministers one cannot extend sincerity and fairness, but instead suspects and guards against them, and on a moment's groundless talk hastily enters men into guilt, making the realm stand as if on tiptoe and look askance—there is absolutely no such form of government.
translations.idiomatic: If entrusted ministers cannot be met with sincerity but are met with suspicion, and a moment's groundless rumor is enough to convict them, so that the realm stands in fear and looks askance—such is not my way of rule.

sentences.zh: 錫寶未察虛實，以書生拘迂之見，託為正言陳奏。

translations.literal: Xibao did not investigate truth and falsehood, and with a pedantic scholar's narrow view offered this as upright speech in memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Xibao failed to verify the facts and, in a pedantic scholar's narrow view, offered the memorial as upright remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 姑寬其罰，改革職留任。

translations.literal: For the moment his punishment was leniently reduced; he was transferred in office but retained in post.
translations.idiomatic: His punishment was leniently reduced and he was transferred but allowed to remain in office.

sentences.zh: 」五十七年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1792.

sentences.zh: 仁宗親政，誅和珅，並籍全家，乃追思錫寶直言，諭曰：「故御史曹錫寶，嘗劾和珅奴劉全倚勢營私，家貲豐厚。

translations.literal: When the Jiaqing Emperor took personal rule, Heshen was executed and his whole family was confiscated; then he recalled Xibao's forthright words and issued an edict: "The late Censor Cao Xibao once impeached Heshen's bondservant Liu Quan for relying on power to seek private gain, with household wealth abundant.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jiaqing Emperor took power, executed Heshen, and confiscated his family's property, he recalled Xibao's forthright memorial and said: "The late Censor Cao Xibao once impeached Heshen's bondservant Liu Quan for abusing power for private gain and amassing great wealth.

sentences.zh: 彼時和珅聲勢薰灼，舉朝無一人敢於糾劾，而錫寶獨能抗辭執奏，不愧諍臣。

translations.literal: At that time Heshen's prestige blazed hot; the whole court had not a single man who dared impeach, yet Xibao alone could speak in opposition and firmly memorialize—he did not disgrace the name of remonstrating minister.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Heshen's power was overwhelming and no one in court dared impeach him, yet Xibao alone spoke out and submitted his memorial—worthy indeed of a remonstrating minister.

sentences.zh: 今和珅治罪後，並籍全家，貲產至二十馀萬。

translations.literal: Now after Heshen was punished and his whole family confiscated, property reached more than two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Now, after Heshen's conviction and the confiscation of his household, the seized property exceeded two hundred thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 是錫寶所劾不虛，宜加優獎，以旌直言。

translations.literal: Thus Xibao's impeachment was not false; he should receive added favorable reward to honor forthright speech.
translations.idiomatic: Xibao's charges were vindicated and he should receive special honors to reward his forthrightness.

sentences.zh: 錫寶贈副都御史，其子江視贈官予廕。

translations.literal: Xibao was posthumously granted Vice Censor-in-Chief; his son Jiang Shi was given the posthumous rank for yin privilege.
translations.idiomatic: Xibao was posthumously granted vice censor-in-chief, and his son Jiang Shi received the corresponding inheritance privilege.

sentences.zh: 」錫寶，一士從子，再世居台省，敢言名。

translations.literal: Xibao was a follower of Yishi; two generations dwelt in the censorate and supervising secretariat, famed for daring speech.
translations.idiomatic: Xibao was a follower of Yishi; for two generations his family served in the censorate and gained renown for outspoken remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 家有甕，焚諫草，江嘗乞諸能文者為詩歌，傳一時雲。

translations.literal: The family had a jar in which remonstrance drafts were burned; Jiang once begged literary men to compose poems and songs, which spread for a time like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: The family kept a jar in which remonstrance drafts were burned. Jiang once asked literary men to compose poems about it, and the story spread widely for a time.

sentences.zh: =謝振定=謝振定，字一齋，一字薌泉，湖南湘鄉人。

translations.literal: Xie Zhending, courtesy name Yizhai and also Xiangquan, was a man of Xiangxiang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Zhending, styled Yizhai and also known as Xiangquan, came from Xiangxiang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十五年進士，改庶吉士，散館授編修。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year of Qianlong he became a jinshi, was made a Hanlin bachelor, and upon leaving the academy was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in 1780, entered the Hanlin Academy, and on completing his term was made a compiler.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，考選江南道監察御史。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year he was selected by examination as Censor of the Jiangnan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1794 he was selected by examination as censor of the Jiangnan circuit.

sentences.zh: 巡視南漕，漕艘阻瓜洲，振定禱於神，風轉順漕艘，人稱「謝公風」。

translations.literal: Inspecting the southern grain transport, transport vessels were blocked at Guazhou; Zhending prayed to the spirit, the wind turned favorable for the transport vessels, and people called it "Master Xie's wind."
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting southern grain transport, he found vessels stalled at Guazhou. After Zhending prayed, the wind shifted in their favor, and people called it "Master Xie's wind."

sentences.zh: 六十年，遷兵科給事中。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year he was transferred to Supervising Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1795 he was transferred to supervising secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 巡視東城，有乘違制車騁於衢者，執而訊之，則和珅妾弟也，語不遜，振定命痛笞之，遂焚其車。

translations.literal: Inspecting the eastern city, someone rode an illegal carriage galloping in the street; he seized and questioned him—it was Heshen's brother-in-law by a concubine; his words were insolent; Zhending ordered him severely beaten and then burned his carriage.
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting the eastern city he seized a man driving an illegal carriage recklessly through the streets. It was Heshen's brother-in-law by a concubine, who spoke insolently. Zhending had him beaten severely and burned the carriage.

sentences.zh: 曰：「此車豈堪宰相坐耶？

translations.literal: He said: "How can this carriage be fit for a chief minister to sit in?
translations.idiomatic: He said, "How could a carriage like this be fit for a chief minister?"

sentences.zh: 」居數日，給事中王鍾健希和珅意，假他事劾振定，奪職。

translations.literal: Within several days, Supervising Secretary Wang Zhongjian, hoping to please Heshen, used another matter to impeach Zhending and stripped him of office.
translations.idiomatic: Days later Supervising Secretary Wang Zhongjian, seeking to please Heshen, impeached Zhending on another charge and stripped him of office.

sentences.zh: 和珅敗，嘉慶五年，起授禮部主事。

translations.literal: When Heshen fell, in the fifth year of Jiaqing he was recalled and appointed Principal Clerk in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After Heshen's fall, in 1800 he was recalled and appointed principal clerk in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 遷員外郎，充坐糧廳，監收漕糧，裁革陋規，兌運肅然。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director, served in the Grain Transport Office, supervised collection of transport grain, cut abusive customary fees, and transport exchange became orderly.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director, served in the grain transport office supervising tribute grain collection, abolished abusive customary fees, and restored order to transport operations.

sentences.zh: 十四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1809.

sentences.zh: 道光中，振定子興嶢，官河南裕州知州。

translations.literal: In the Daoguang period, Zhending's son Xingyao served as magistrate of Yuzhou in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daoguang reign, Zhending's son Xingyao served as magistrate of Yuzhou in Henan.

sentences.zh: 以卓薦引見，循例奏姓名、裡貫。

translations.literal: By outstanding recommendation he was presented for audience and, following precedent, reported his name and native place.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended for outstanding service, he was presented at court and, as usual, stated his name and native place.

sentences.zh: 宣宗問：「爾湖南人，乃能為京師語，何也？

translations.literal: The Xuanzong Emperor asked: "You are a Hunan man—how can you speak the capital dialect?
translations.idiomatic: The Xuanzong Emperor asked, "You are from Hunan—how is it that you speak the Beijing dialect?"

sentences.zh: 」興嶢對言：「臣父振定官御史，臣生長京師。

translations.literal: Xingyao replied: "Your servant's father Zhending served as censor; your servant grew up in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyao replied, "My father Zhending served as a censor, and I grew up in Beijing."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「爾乃燒車御史子耶？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "So you are the son of the censor who burned the carriage?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "So you are the son of the censor who burned the carriage?"

sentences.zh: 」因褒勉甚至。

translations.literal: Thereupon he praised and encouraged him to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: He praised and encouraged him warmly.

sentences.zh: 明日，語軍機大臣：「朕少聞燒車御史事，昨乃見其子。

translations.literal: The next day he told the Grand Council members: "I heard little of the censor who burned the carriage when young; yesterday I met his son.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he told the Grand Council, "I had heard little of the censor who burned the carriage in my youth; yesterday I met his son."

sentences.zh: 」命擢興嶢敘州知府。

translations.literal: He ordered Xingyao promoted to Prefect of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted Xingyao to prefect of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: =錢灃=錢灃，字東注，雲南昆明人。

translations.literal: Qian Feng, courtesy name Dongzhu, was a man of Kunming in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Feng, styled Dongzhu, came from Kunming in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十六年進士，改庶吉士，散館授檢討。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year of Qianlong he became a jinshi, was made a Hanlin bachelor, and upon leaving the academy was appointed Reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in 1771, entered the Hanlin Academy, and on completing his term was made a reviser.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，考選江南道監察御史。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year he was selected by examination as Censor of the Jiangnan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1781 he was selected by examination as censor of the Jiangnan circuit.

sentences.zh: 甘肅冒賑折捐事發，主其事者為甘肅布政使王亶望，時已遷浙江巡撫，坐誅，總督勒爾謹及諸府縣吏死者數十人，事具亶望傳。

translations.literal: The Gansu false relief and diverted donation affair broke out; the man in charge was Gansu Provincial Administration Commissioner Wang Danwang, who had already been transferred to Zhejiang governor and was executed; Governor-General Le'erjin and dozens of prefectural and county officials died—the matter is fully set forth in Danwang's biography.
translations.idiomatic: When the Gansu false relief and diverted-donation scandal broke, its chief culprit was Provincial Administration Commissioner Wang Danwang, by then transferred to Zhejiang as governor. He was executed, along with Governor-General Le'erjin and dozens of prefectural and county officials. The affair is recorded in Wang's biography.

sentences.zh: 陝西巡撫畢沅嘗兩署陝甘總督，獨置不問。

translations.literal: Shaanxi Governor Bi Yuan had twice acted as Shaanxi-Gansu Governor-General, yet was alone left unquestioned.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi Governor Bi Yuan had twice served as acting Shaanxi-Gansu governor-general, yet went unpunished.

sentences.zh: 灃疏言：「冒賑折捐，固由亶望骫法，但亶望為布政使時，沅兩署總督，近在同城，豈無聞見？

translations.literal: Feng memorialized: "The false relief and diverted donation was indeed due to Danwang's bending the law, but when Danwang was provincial administration commissioner, Yuan twice acted as governor-general in the same city nearby—how could he have had no knowledge?
translations.idiomatic: Feng memorialized: "The false relief and diverted donations were certainly Wang Danwang's crime, but while Wang was provincial administration commissioner, Bi Yuan twice served as acting governor-general in the same city—could he really have known nothing?"

sentences.zh: 使沅早發其奸，則播惡不至如此之甚；

translations.literal: If Yuan had early exposed the crime, the spread of evil would not have reached such severity;
translations.idiomatic: Had Bi Yuan exposed the fraud early, the scandal would not have spread so widely;

sentences.zh: 即陷於刑闢者，亦不至如此之多。

translations.literal: even those who fell under punishment would not have been so many.
translations.idiomatic: nor would so many officials have been condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 臣不敢謂其利令智昏，甘受所餌，惟是瞻徇回護，不肯舉發，甚非大臣居心之道。

translations.literal: Your servant does not dare say he was blinded by profit and took bait willingly, but only that he looked up and yielded in protection, unwilling to report—this is very far from the way a great minister should conduct his mind.
translations.idiomatic: I do not claim he was blinded by profit and accepted bribes, only that he looked the other way and refused to report the crime—conduct unworthy of a senior minister.

sentences.zh: 請比捏結各員治罪。

translations.literal: I beg that he be punished like those who fabricated cases.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that he be punished like the officials who fabricated cases."

sentences.zh: 」上為詰責沅，降秩視三品，事具沅傳。

translations.literal: The Emperor rebuked and censured Yuan, reduced his rank to treated as third grade—the matter is fully set forth in Yuan's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor rebuked Bi Yuan and reduced his rank to third grade. The affair is recorded in his biography.

sentences.zh: 四十七年，灃疏劾山東巡撫國泰、布政使於易簡吏治廢弛，貪婪無饜，各州縣庫皆虧缺，上命大學士和珅、左都御史劉墉率灃往按。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year Feng memorialized to impeach Shandong Governor Guotai and Provincial Administration Commissioner Yu Yijian for lax governance, insatiable greed, and deficits in every prefectural and county treasury; the Emperor ordered Grand Secretary Heshen and Left Censor-in-Chief Liu Yong to lead Feng to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: In 1782 Feng impeached Shandong Governor Guotai and Provincial Administration Commissioner Yu Yijian for lax governance, insatiable greed, and deficits in prefectural and county treasuries. The Emperor sent Grand Secretary Heshen and Left Censor-in-Chief Liu Yong to investigate, with Feng accompanying them.

sentences.zh: 和珅庇國泰，怵灃，灃不為撓。

translations.literal: Heshen shielded Guotai and intimidated Feng, but Feng was not swayed.
translations.idiomatic: Heshen shielded Guotai and tried to intimidate Feng, but Feng would not yield.

sentences.zh: 至山東，發歷城縣庫驗帑銀。

translations.literal: Arriving in Shandong, they opened the Licheng county treasury to verify reserve silver.
translations.idiomatic: In Shandong they opened the Licheng county treasury to verify the reserve silver.

sentences.zh: 故事，帑銀以五十兩為一鋌，市銀則否。

translations.literal: By precedent, reserve silver came in ingots of fifty taels each; market silver did not.
translations.idiomatic: By regulation, reserve silver was cast in fifty-tael ingots, unlike ordinary market silver.

sentences.zh: 國泰聞使者將至，假市銀補庫。

translations.literal: Guotai, hearing the envoys were coming, used borrowed market silver to fill the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that investigators were coming, Guotai filled the treasury with borrowed market silver.

sentences.zh: 灃按問得其狀，召商還所假，庫為之空。

translations.literal: Feng investigated and obtained the facts, summoned the merchants to return what had been borrowed, and the treasury was emptied thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Feng established the facts, ordered the merchants to reclaim their silver, and the treasury was left empty.

sentences.zh: 复按章丘、東平、益都三州縣庫，皆虧缺如灃言。

translations.literal: Again they inspected the treasuries of Zhangqiu, Dongping, and Yidu—the three prefectures and counties—and all showed deficits as Feng had said.
translations.idiomatic: Further inspections of the Zhangqiu, Dongping, and Yidu treasuries confirmed Feng's charges of widespread deficits.

sentences.zh: 國泰、易簡罪至死，和珅不能護也。

translations.literal: Guotai and Yijian were guilty to the death penalty; Heshen could not protect them.
translations.idiomatic: Guotai and Yu Yijian were sentenced to death, and even Heshen could not protect them.

sentences.zh: 上旌灃直言，擢通政司參議。

translations.literal: The Emperor honored Feng's forthright speech and promoted him to Counselor of the Court of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor commended Feng's forthrightness and promoted him to counselor of the Court of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，遷太常寺少卿。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In 1783 he was transferred to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 再遷通政司副使。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Vice Commissioner of the Court of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again, to vice commissioner of the Court of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 出督湖南學政，灃持正，得士為盛。

translations.literal: He went out to supervise Hunan education; Feng was upright, and the scholars he obtained flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Posted as educational commissioner for Hunan, he upheld standards rigorously and produced many distinguished scholars.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，任滿，命留任。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year, when his term ended, he was ordered to remain in office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1786, when his term ended, he was ordered to remain in office.

sentences.zh: 湖北荊州水壞城郭，孝感土豪殺饑民。

translations.literal: In Hubei, Jingzhou's walls were destroyed by floodwaters, and in Xiaogan local bullies killed famine victims.
translations.idiomatic: Floods destroyed the walls of Jingzhou in Hubei, and local bullies in Xiaogan killed famine victims.

sentences.zh: 上責灃在鄰省何不以聞，下部議。

translations.literal: The Emperor rebuked Feng for being in a neighboring province and not reporting it, and handed the case to the ministry for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor rebuked Feng for failing to report the affair from a neighboring province and referred the case to the ministries.

sentences.zh: 諸生或匿喪赴試，又有上違禁書籍者。

translations.literal: Some licentiates concealed mourning to take examinations, and some presented forbidden books.
translations.idiomatic: Some licentiates concealed mourning to sit examinations, and others submitted forbidden books.

sentences.zh: 灃按治未竟，聞親喪去官，以事屬巡撫浦霖。

translations.literal: Feng's investigation was not yet finished when he heard of a parent's death and left office; the matter belonged to Governor Pulin.
translations.idiomatic: Before Feng could finish the investigation he left office upon a parent's death, leaving the matter to Governor Pulin.

sentences.zh: 霖遂並劾灃，坐奪職。

translations.literal: Pulin then also impeached Feng, and he was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Pulin then impeached Feng as well, and Feng was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 上命左授六部主事。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered him demoted-left to Principal Clerk in one of the Six Ministries.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor demoted him to principal clerk in one of the Six Ministries.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，灃服除，詣京師，授戶部主事。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year, when Feng's mourning ended, he went to the capital and was appointed Principal Clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In 1793, after his mourning period ended, he went to Beijing and was appointed principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 引見，即擢員外郎。

translations.literal: On presentation for audience he was immediately promoted to Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: At his audience he was immediately promoted to vice director.

sentences.zh: 复除湖廣道監察御史。

translations.literal: Again he was appointed Censor of the Huguang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed censor of the Huguang circuit.

sentences.zh: 時和珅愈專政，大學士阿桂、王杰，尚書董誥、福長安與同為軍機大臣，不相能，入直恆異處。

translations.literal: At the time Heshen increasingly monopolized government; Grand Secretaries Agui and Wang Jie and Ministers Dong Gao and Fu Chang'an were together Grand Council members but could not get along, and when entering duty they constantly stayed in different places.
translations.idiomatic: Heshen was then tightening his grip on power. Grand Secretaries Agui and Wang Jie and Ministers Dong Gao and Fu Chang'an all served on the Grand Council but could not work together, and even on duty they kept to separate quarters.

sentences.zh: 灃疏言：「我朝設立軍機處，大臣與其職者，皆萃止其中，庸以集思廣益，仰贊高深。

translations.literal: Feng memorialized: "Our dynasty established the Grand Council so that ministers holding its duties would all gather and stop within it, thereby to collect thoughts and broaden benefits and look up to assist the exalted and profound.
translations.idiomatic: Feng memorialized: "The Grand Council was established so that all council ministers would work together in one place, pooling counsel to assist Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 地一則勢無所分，居同則情可共見。

translations.literal: With one place, power has nowhere to divide; dwelling together, sentiments can be jointly seen.
translations.idiomatic: A single workplace prevents divided authority, and working together allows motives to be seen clearly.

sentences.zh: 即各司諮事畫，亦有定所。

translations.literal: Even when each ministry consults on matters for drafting, there are fixed places.
translations.idiomatic: Even when ministries submit drafts for consultation, there are fixed places for doing so.

sentences.zh: 近日惟阿桂每日入止軍機處；

translations.literal: Recently only Agui daily enters and stops at the Grand Council;
translations.idiomatic: Lately only Agui works daily in the Grand Council offices;

sentences.zh: 和珅或止內右門內直廬，或止隆宗門外近造辦處直廬；

translations.literal: Heshen sometimes stops only at the inner duty lodge inside the Inner Right Gate, or only at the duty lodge near the Manufacturing Office outside Longzong Gate;
translations.idiomatic: Heshen sometimes works only at the inner duty lodge by the Inner Right Gate or at the lodge near the Manufacturing Office outside Longzong Gate;

sentences.zh: 王杰、董誥則止於南書房；

translations.literal: Wang Jie and Dong Gao stop only at the Southern Study;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jie and Dong Gao work only in the Southern Study;

sentences.zh: 福長安則止於造辦處。

translations.literal: Fu Chang'an stops only at the Manufacturing Office.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Chang'an works only at the Manufacturing Office.

sentences.zh: 每日召對，聯行而入，退即各還所處。

translations.literal: Each day when summoned for audience they enter in a group, and on retiring each returns to his own place.
translations.idiomatic: They enter the palace together for daily audiences, then withdraw each to his own quarters.

sentences.zh: 雖亦有時暫至軍機處，而事過輒起。

translations.literal: Although they also sometimes go temporarily to the Grand Council, when the matter passes they immediately rise and leave.
translations.idiomatic: Although they sometimes visit the Grand Council briefly, they leave as soon as the business is done."

sentences.zh: 各司諮事畫，趨步多歧。

translations.literal: When each ministry consults on drafting documents, the steps taken go in many directions.
translations.idiomatic: When ministries submit drafts for consultation, ministers scatter in different directions.

sentences.zh: 皇上乾行之健，離照之明，大小臣工戴德懷刑，浹於肌髓，決不至因此遂啟朋黨角立之漸。

translations.literal: The Emperor's vigorous movement like Heaven, the brilliance of departing radiance—great and small officials wear virtue and carry punishment in their hearts, penetrating marrow, and will by no means on this account thereby begin the first signs of factional corners standing against one another.
translations.idiomatic: With Your Majesty's firm resolve and penetrating judgment, officials at every rank are steeped in gratitude and awe; this will by no means be the seed of factional rivalry.

sentences.zh: 然世宗憲皇帝以來，及皇上御極之久，軍機大臣萃止無渙，未嘗纖芥有他。

translations.literal: Yet since Emperor Shizong the August and through the long years of Your Majesty's reign, Grand Council ministers have gathered and stopped without dispersal, never having so much as a fiber of difference elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Yongzheng reign and throughout Your Majesty's long rule, Grand Council ministers have always worked together without splitting off—even for the smallest matter.

sentences.zh: 由前律後，不應聽其輕更。

translations.literal: Taking what went before as the rule for what follows, one should not allow this lightly to be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Established practice should not be lightly abandoned.

sentences.zh: 內右門內切近禁寢，向因有養心殿帶領引見事，須先一兩刻預備。

translations.literal: Inside the Inner Right Gate is close to the forbidden sleeping quarters; formerly because there were matters of leading presentations at the Hall of Mental Cultivation, one or two quarter-hours in advance were needed for preparation.
translations.idiomatic: The Inner Right Gate lies very close to the imperial apartments; ministers had to arrive early to prepare for audiences at the Hall of Mental Cultivation.

sentences.zh: 恩加大臣，不令與各官露立，是以設廬許得暫止。

translations.literal: Favor was extended to ministers, not letting them stand exposed in the open like other officials, and therefore lodges were set up allowing temporary stopping.
translations.idiomatic: As a special favor, ministers were spared standing in the open like other officials and were allowed temporary lodging nearby.

sentences.zh: 不應於未辨色之前，一大臣入止，而隨從軍機司員亦更入更出。

translations.literal: One should not, before dawn can be distinguished, have one minister enter and stop while attendant Grand Council clerks also come in and go out in alternation.
translations.idiomatic: A single minister should not lodge inside before dawn while Grand Council clerks come and go freely.

sentences.zh: 為日既久，不能不與內監相狎。

translations.literal: As the days lengthen, they cannot but become familiar with eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Over time they inevitably grow too familiar with palace eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 萬一有無知如高雲從者，雖立正刑闢，而所絓已多，杜漸宜早。

translations.literal: If by chance there should be someone ignorant like Gao Yuncong, although upright punishment could be applied to purge him, the entanglements would already be many; cutting it off early is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Even if a scoundrel like Gao Yuncong were punished, much harm might already be done—prevention is better than cure.

sentences.zh: 至南書房備幾暇顧問，俟軍機事畢，入直未遲；

translations.literal: As for the Southern Study prepared for leisure consultation, waiting until Grand Council business is finished to enter duty would not be late;
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Study can serve for consultation after Grand Council work is done; there is no need to go there beforehand.

sentences.zh: 若隆宗門外直廬及造辦處，則各色應差皆得覘聽於外，大臣於中治事，亦屬過褻。

translations.literal: If at the duty lodge outside Longzong Gate and the Manufacturing Office, then officials of every sort on duty outside can peep and listen, while ministers conduct affairs within—this also counts as overly familiar.
translations.idiomatic: At the lodges outside Longzong Gate or the Manufacturing Office, all sorts of attendants can overhear ministers at work—far too loose an arrangement.

sentences.zh: 請敕諸大臣仍照舊規同止軍機處，庶匪懈之忱，各申五夜；

translations.literal: I request that an edict order all ministers still according to the old rule to stop together at the Grand Council, so that the sincerity of not being lax may each extend through five watches;
translations.idiomatic: Please command all ministers to resume gathering at the Grand Council as before, so each may give his full diligence through the night watches.

sentences.zh: 協恭之雅，共勵一堂。

translations.literal: The elegance of harmonious respect, together encouraging one another in one hall.
translations.idiomatic: They can work harmoniously together under one roof.

sentences.zh: 其圓明園治事，和珅、福長安止於如意門外南順牆東向直廬，王杰、董誥止於南書房直廬，並請敕更正。

translations.literal: As for conducting affairs at the Old Summer Palace, Heshen and Fu Chang'an stop only at the east-facing duty lodge south along the wall outside Ruyi Gate; Wang Jie and Dong Gao stop only at the Southern Study duty lodge—both please order corrected by edict.
translations.idiomatic: At the Old Summer Palace, Heshen and Fu Chang'an work only at the lodge south of Ruyi Gate, while Wang Jie and Dong Gao use the Southern Study lodge—please order these arrangements corrected as well.

sentences.zh: 」上為申誡諸大臣，並命灃稽察軍機處。

translations.literal: " The Emperor on this account admonished the ministers, and also ordered Feng to inspect the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor admonished the ministers accordingly and ordered Feng to inspect the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 和珅素惡灃，至是尤深嗛之。

translations.literal: Heshen had always hated Feng; at this point he especially deeply resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Heshen had long disliked Feng, and now hated him all the more.

sentences.zh: 上夙許其持正，度未可遽傾，凡遇勞苦事多委之。

translations.literal: The Emperor had long approved his uprightness; estimating he could not quickly be overthrown, whenever encountering arduous tasks he entrusted many to him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had long valued Feng's integrity and knew he could not easily be brought down; difficult assignments were often entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 灃貧，衣裘薄，宵興晡散，遂得疾。

translations.literal: Feng was poor; his fur garments were thin; rising at night and dispersing at dusk—he consequently fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: Feng was poor and thinly clothed; rising before dawn and working until evening, he fell ill.

sentences.zh: 六十年，卒。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In 1795 he died.

sentences.zh: 或謂灃將劾和珅，和珅實酖之。

translations.literal: Some say Feng was about to impeach Heshen, and Heshen actually poisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Some claimed Feng was preparing to impeach Heshen and that Heshen had him poisoned.

sentences.zh: =尹壯圖=尹壯圖，字楚珍，雲南昆明人。

translations.literal: Yin Zhuangtu — Yin Zhuangtu, courtesy name Chuzhen, was a man of Kunming in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhuangtu, styled Chuzhen, came from Kunming in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十一年進士，改庶吉士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the thirty-first year of Qianlong; transferred to Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in 1766 and entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor.

sentences.zh: 散館，授禮部主事。

translations.literal: Upon leaving the academy, he was appointed Principal Clerk in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After completing Hanlin training he was appointed principal clerk in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 再遷郎中。

translations.literal: He was promoted again to Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to director.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，考選江南道監察御史，轉京畿道。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year, selected by examination as Censor of the Jiangnan Circuit, transferred to the Capital Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1774 he was selected as censor of the Jiangnan circuit and then transferred to the Capital circuit.

sentences.zh: 三遷至內閣學士，兼禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Promoted three times to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat, concurrently Vice Minister of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he became grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat and concurrently vice minister of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 高宗季年，督撫坐譴，或令繳罰項貸罪，壯圖以為非政體。

translations.literal: In the late years of Gaozong, governors-general and governors who incurred censure were sometimes ordered to pay fines in lieu of punishment; Zhuangtu considered this not proper governance.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong's later years, censured governors were often allowed to pay fines instead of facing dismissal; Zhuangtu regarded this as bad policy.

sentences.zh: 五十五年，上疏言：「督撫自蹈愆尤，聖恩不即罷斥，罰銀若干萬充公，亦有督撫自請認罰若干萬者。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fifth year, he submitted a memorial saying: "Governors-general and governors who themselves fall into faults, receiving imperial grace without immediate dismissal, pay fines of several hundred thousand taels for the public treasury; there are also governors who themselves request to acknowledge fines of several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In 1790 he memorialized: "When governors err, imperial grace spares them immediate dismissal and they pay fines of many thousands of taels to the treasury—some even volunteer such payments.

sentences.zh: 在桀驁者藉口以快其饕餮之私，即清廉者亦不得不望屬員之佽助。

translations.literal: Among the arrogant, they use this as a pretext to satisfy their gluttonous private desires; even the incorrupt must still look to subordinate officials for mutual aid.
translations.idiomatic: The corrupt seize on the practice to enrich themselves, while even honest officials must lean on subordinates for help.

sentences.zh: 日後遇有虧空營私重案，不容不曲為庇護。

translations.literal: Later when encountering major cases of deficit and private profit, they cannot but bend to shield them.
translations.idiomatic: When major cases of embezzlement arise later, they cannot but cover for one another.

sentences.zh: 是罰銀雖嚴，不惟無以動其愧懼之心，且潛生其玩易之念，請永停此例。

translations.literal: Thus although the fine in silver is severe, not only does it fail to move their hearts of shame and fear, but it also secretly breeds the thought of treating matters lightly; I request that this precedent be permanently stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Fines may look severe, but they neither inspire remorse nor deter abuse—they encourage complacency. I urge that this practice be abolished permanently.

sentences.zh: 如才具平常者，或即罷斥，或用京職，毋許再膺外任。

translations.literal: If their talent is ordinary, either dismiss them immediately or employ them in capital posts; do not permit them again to hold outside appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Mediocre officials should be dismissed or given capital posts and barred from provincial office.

sentences.zh: 」上諭曰：「壯圖請停罰銀例，不為無見。

translations.literal: " The Emperor instructed: "Zhuangtu's request to stop the fine-in-silver precedent is not without insight.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor replied: "Zhuangtu's call to end the fine system is not without merit.

sentences.zh: 朕以督撫一時不能得人，棄瑕錄用，酌示薄懲。

translations.literal: I, because governors-general and governors could not for the moment obtain the right men, discarded flaws and employed them, showing measured light punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Good provincial leaders were hard to find, so I overlooked flaws and imposed modest fines instead of dismissal.

sentences.zh: 但督撫等或有昧良負恩，以措辦官項為辭，需索屬員；

translations.literal: But governors-general and governors and the like may perhaps be ungrateful and fail their benefactor, using arranging official funds as a pretext to demand from subordinate officials;
translations.idiomatic: Yet some governors may abuse the system, using the need to raise fines as a pretext to squeeze their subordinates;

sentences.zh: 而屬員亦藉此斂派逢迎，此亦不能保其必無。

translations.literal: And subordinate officials also use this to levy collections and curry favor—this too cannot be guaranteed never to occur.
translations.idiomatic: and subordinates may levy exactions in turn to please their superiors—I cannot guarantee this never happens.

sentences.zh: 壯圖既為此奏，自必確有見聞，令指實覆奏。

translations.literal: Since Zhuangtu has made this memorial, he must surely have concrete knowledge; order him to report with specific facts.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhuangtu raised this charge, he must have evidence—order him to substantiate it in a follow-up memorial.

sentences.zh: 」壯圖覆奏：「各督撫聲名狼藉，吏治廢弛。

translations.literal: " Zhuangtu replied: "Every governor-general and governor has a disordered reputation; official governance is lax and slack.
