translations.idiomatic: Zhuangtu replied: "Provincial governors are widely discredited and local administration is in decline.

sentences.zh: 臣經過地方，體察官吏賢否，商民半皆蹙額興嘆。

translations.literal: Passing through places on my route, I inspected whether officials were worthy or not; merchants and commoners were half and half all knitting brows and sighing in lament.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever I traveled I found officials wanting, and merchants and townspeople everywhere knit their brows and sigh.

sentences.zh: 各省風氣，大抵皆然。

translations.literal: The atmosphere in each province is largely all like this.
translations.idiomatic: The same conditions prevail in every province.

sentences.zh: 請旨簡派滿洲大臣同臣往各省密查虧空。

translations.literal: I request an imperial order to select and dispatch Manchu ministers together with me to each province secretly to inspect deficits.
translations.idiomatic: I request that Manchu ministers be appointed to accompany me on a secret audit of provincial treasuries.

sentences.zh: 」上复諭曰：「壯圖覆奏，並未指實。

translations.literal: " The Emperor again instructed: "Zhuangtu's reply memorial still has not cited concrete facts.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor replied again: "Zhuangtu's follow-up still lacks specifics.

sentences.zh: 至稱經過諸省商民蹙額興嘆，竟似居今之世，民不堪命。

translations.literal: As for saying that passing through provinces merchants knit brows and sigh, it is as if living in the present age the people cannot bear their fate.
translations.idiomatic: To claim that merchants everywhere knit their brows and sigh makes it sound as if the people can no longer endure their lot under your reign.

sentences.zh: 此聞自何人，見於何處，仍令指實覆奏。

translations.literal: This report came from what person, seen in what place—again order specific facts in the reply memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Name your informants and the places you saw this—submit another specific memorial.

sentences.zh: 」壯圖再覆奏，自承措詞過當，請治罪。

translations.literal: " Zhuangtu again replied, himself acknowledging excessive wording, requesting punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangtu replied once more, admitting his language was excessive and asking to be punished.

sentences.zh: 上命戶部侍郎慶成偕壯圖赴山西察倉庫，始大同府庫，次山西布政使庫，皆無虧。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Vice Minister of Revenue Qingcheng together with Zhuangtu to go to Shanxi to inspect treasuries, first the Datong prefectural treasury, next the Shanxi provincial treasury—all without deficit.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Vice Minister Qingcheng with Zhuangtu to inspect Shanxi treasuries, starting with Datong and the provincial treasury—no deficits were found.

sentences.zh: 壯圖請還京治罪。

translations.literal: Zhuangtu requested return to the capital for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangtu asked to return to Beijing to accept punishment.

sentences.zh: 上命慶成偕壯圖再赴直隸、山東、江南諸省。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Qingcheng together with Zhuangtu again to proceed to Zhili, Shandong, Jiangnan, and other provinces.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered them to continue the inspection in Zhili, Shandong, Jiangnan, and other provinces.

sentences.zh: 慶成所至，輒遊宴數日，乃發倉庫校覈，歷直隸布政使及正定、蘭山、山陽諸府縣，皆無虧。

translations.literal: Wherever Qingcheng arrived, he would immediately feast and banquet for several days, then only after that open treasuries for verification; passing through the Zhili provincial treasury and Zhengding, Lanshan, Shanyang, and other prefectures and counties—all without deficit.
translations.idiomatic: Qingcheng spent days feasting at each stop before inspecting treasuries; from Zhili through Zhengding, Lanshan, Shanyang, and elsewhere, none showed deficits.

sentences.zh: 上寄諭壯圖，問途中見商民蹙額興嘆狀否。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent a private instruction to Zhuangtu, asking whether on the road he saw the condition of merchants knitting brows and sighing.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor privately asked Zhuangtu whether he had seen merchants knitting their brows and sighing along the way.

sentences.zh: 壯圖覆奏，言目見商民樂業，絕無蹙額興嘆情事。

translations.literal: Zhuangtu replied, saying with his own eyes he saw merchants happily pursuing their trades; there was absolutely none of the affair of knitting brows and sighing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangtu replied that merchants appeared content at their trades and showed no sign of distress.

sentences.zh: 上又令慶成傳旨，令其指實二三人，毋更含糊支飾。

translations.literal: The Emperor again ordered Qingcheng to transmit the edict, ordering him to name two or three persons concretely, not again to be vague and evasive.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had Qingcheng instruct him to name two or three specific examples and stop evading the question.

sentences.zh: 壯圖自承虛誑，奏請治罪。

translations.literal: Zhuangtu himself acknowledged falsehood, memorialized requesting punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangtu admitted his claims were false and asked to be punished.

sentences.zh: 尋复察蘇州布政使庫，亦無虧。

translations.literal: Soon after, again inspecting the Suzhou provincial treasury—also no deficit.
translations.idiomatic: The Suzhou provincial treasury was inspected as well and found in order.

sentences.zh: 還京，下刑部治罪，比挾詐欺公、妄生異議律，坐斬決。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, handed to the Ministry of Justice for punishment; compared to the statute on using fraud to deceive the public and recklessly generating dissent, sentenced to decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Beijing he was tried by the Ministry of Justice under the statutes on fraud and fomenting dissent, and sentenced to decapitation.

sentences.zh: 上謂壯圖逞臆妄言，亦不妨以謗為規，不必遽加重罪，命左授內閣侍讀。

translations.literal: The Emperor said Zhuangtu spoke recklessly from imagination, yet also it was not improper to take slander as remonstrance; there was no need hastily to add heavy punishment—ordered demoted-left to Hanlin Reader in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor judged that though Zhuangtu had spoken rashly, his criticism need not be treated as a capital crime and demoted him to Hanlin reader.

sentences.zh: 繼又以侍讀缺少，改禮部主事。

translations.literal: Subsequently, because the reader post was vacant, changed to Principal Clerk in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Later, with no reader vacancy available, he was made principal clerk in the Ministry of Rites instead.

sentences.zh: 壯圖以母老乞歸。

translations.literal: Zhuangtu, because his mother was old, requested leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangtu asked to retire to care for his elderly mother.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年，仁宗親政，召詣京師。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing, when Renzong personally governed, summoned to proceed to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In 1799, when the Jiaqing Emperor took direct rule, Zhuangtu was summoned to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 壯圖仍以母老乞歸，上賜其母大緞兩端，加壯圖給事中銜，賜奏事摺匣，命得上章言事。

translations.literal: Zhuangtu still, because his mother was old, requested return home; the Emperor bestowed on his mother two bolts of large satin, added Zhuangtu the title of Supervising Secretary, bestowed a memorial folding case, and ordered that he might submit memorials to speak on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangtu again pleaded his elderly mother; the Emperor gave his mother two bolts of fine satin, granted Zhuangtu the rank of supervising secretary, and presented him with a memorial case so he could continue to report to the throne.

sentences.zh: 壯圖未行，复上疏請清覈各省陋規，明定科條，上以為不可行。

translations.literal: Before Zhuangtu departed, again submitted a memorial requesting thorough audit of irregular fees in each province and clear establishment of regulations; the Emperor considered it not feasible.
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving, Zhuangtu again memorialized to abolish illicit provincial fees and define clear rules; the Emperor rejected the proposal.

sentences.zh: 既歸，疏請拔真才，儲實用，大要謂：「保舉未定處分，當下吏部嚴立科條；

translations.literal: Having returned home, he memorialized requesting selection of true talent and storage of practical use; the main points said: "For recommendations with undetermined penalties, the Ministry of Personnel should strictly establish regulations;
translations.idiomatic: After returning home he memorialized on recruiting talent, arguing in essence: "Rules for recommendation and punishment should be set by the Ministry of Personnel;

sentences.zh: 科埸或通關節，當將房考落卷送主司搜閱。

translations.literal: If in the examination hall there should be leaked connections, the failed papers from examining-room graders should be sent to the chief examiner for search and review.
translations.idiomatic: When exam fraud is suspected, failed papers from room examiners should be forwarded to the chief examiner for review.

sentences.zh: 其尤要者，謂六部滿洲司員案，文義多未曉暢，當嚴督令習經書通文理；

translations.literal: What is especially important is that among the Manchu clerks in the Six Ministries, many do not understand literary meaning clearly; they should be strictly supervised to study the classics and comprehend literary principles;
translations.idiomatic: Most urgently, Manchu clerks in the Six Ministries often lack literary competence and should be required to master the classics;

sentences.zh: 鄉會試加廣名額，司員先侭科甲挑補。

translations.literal: Add expanded quotas for provincial and metropolitan examinations; clerks should first be selected and supplemented from those who passed civil examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Expand examination quotas and fill clerkships preferentially with degree-holders.

sentences.zh: 」下軍機大臣議，奏謂惟房考落卷送主司搜閱，事近可行，補入科場條例。

translations.literal: " Referred to Grand Council ministers for deliberation; they memorialized saying only sending failed papers from room examiners to the chief examiner for search and review was nearly feasible, and added this to examination regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Council considered the proposals and approved only forwarding failed examination papers to chief examiners, which was incorporated into examination regulations.

sentences.zh: 雲南巡撫初彭齡乞養歸，壯圖疏請留，上不允。

translations.literal: Yunnan Governor Chu Pengling requested leave to return home to care for parents; Zhuangtu memorialized requesting he be kept; the Emperor did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: When Yunnan Governor Chu Pengling asked to retire to care for his parents, Zhuangtu urged that he be retained; the Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 別疏復申前議，謂滿洲子弟十五六歲前專責習經書通文理，再習騎射繙譯。

translations.literal: In a separate memorial he again set forth the previous proposal, saying Manchu youths before fifteen or sixteen should be solely charged to study classics and master literary principles, then study horsemanship, archery, and translation.
translations.idiomatic: In another memorial he renewed his earlier proposal that Manchu youths should study the classics before age fifteen or sixteen, then horsemanship, archery, and translation.

sentences.zh: 上謂：「壯圖以前嘗駁飭之事復行瀆陳，更張本朝成法。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Zhuangtu again presents in a tiresome manner matters previously rebuked and admonished, altering longstanding institutions of our dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Zhuangtu is harping again on proposals already rejected and trying to overturn established dynastic practice.

sentences.zh: 下雲南巡撫伊桑阿傳旨申飭。

translations.literal: Sent down to Yunnan Governor Yisang'a to transmit the edict and admonish him.
translations.idiomatic: The rebuke was relayed to Yunnan Governor Yisang'a for transmission to Zhuangtu.

sentences.zh: 」八年，疏言：「天下萬幾，皆皇上獨理。

translations.literal: " In the eighth year, he memorialized: "The myriad affairs under Heaven are all handled solely by the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1803 he memorialized: "The myriad affairs of empire fall entirely on Your Majesty alone.

sentences.zh: 內外諸臣不過浮沉旅進旅退之中，無能匡扶弼亮。

translations.literal: Inner and outer officials merely float and sink, coming and going in passing, with none able to support, assist, and illuminate.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials drift through office unable to support or advise Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 請於內之卿貳、翰詹、科道，外之籓、臬、道、府，慎選二十人，輪直內廷。

translations.literal: I request from within—vice ministers, Hanlin and compilers, censors—and from without—provincial governors, provincial judicial commissioners, circuit intendants, and prefects—carefully to select twenty people to rotate duty in the inner court.
translations.idiomatic: Select twenty capable officials from among vice ministers, Hanlin scholars, censors, and provincial administrators to serve rotating duty in the inner court.

sentences.zh: 每日奏章諭旨，盡心檢校，有疏忽偏倚之處，許就近詳辨可否。

translations.literal: Daily memorials and imperial instructions—examine them with full heart; where there is neglect or partial bias, permit detailed nearby discussion of whether they may proceed.
translations.idiomatic: Each day they should review memorials and edicts and discuss on the spot any errors or partiality they find.

sentences.zh: 」上責：「壯圖言皆迂闊紕謬，斷不可行。

translations.literal: " The Emperor rebuked: "Zhuangtu's words are all impractical, broad, and erroneous—absolutely not feasible.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor retorted: "Zhuangtu's proposals are impractical and absurd—they cannot be adopted.

sentences.zh: 若如所奏，直於軍機大臣外復設內軍機，成何政體？

translations.literal: If as memorialized, directly outside Grand Council ministers again setting up an inner Grand Council—what sort of governance would that make?
translations.idiomatic: As he proposes it, you would be creating a second Grand Council inside the palace—what kind of government would that be?

sentences.zh: 」因及雲南布政使陳孝升、道員薩榮安方以冒銷軍需被罪，令巡撫那彥寶詰壯圖，何無一言奏及。

translations.literal: " Thereupon mentioning Yunnan Provincial Administration Commissioner Chen Xiaosheng and Circuit Intendant Sa Rong'an, who had just been punished for falsely claiming military supplies expenses, ordered Governor Nayenbao to interrogate Zhuangtu: why was there not one word in memorials about this?
translations.idiomatic: He also asked why Zhuangtu had said nothing about Yunnan officials Chen Xiaosheng and Sa Rong'an, who had just been convicted of falsifying military accounts, and ordered Governor Nayenbao to question him.

sentences.zh: 壯圖言以不得孝升等確據，未敢入告，仍請議處，上命寬之。

translations.literal: Zhuangtu said because he had not obtained solid evidence on Xiaosheng and the rest, he did not dare to report; still requesting deliberation on punishment—the Emperor ordered leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangtu replied that lacking solid evidence on Chen and the others he had not reported them, but still asked to be punished; the Emperor pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 十三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In 1808 he died.

sentences.zh: =【論】=論曰：高宗中年後，遇有言事者，遣大臣按治，輒命其參與。

translations.literal: Commentary says: After Gaozong's middle years, when there were those who spoke on affairs, he dispatched ministers to investigate—and always ordered the memorialist to participate.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: After Qianlong's mid-reign, when an official spoke out on a matter the Emperor would send ministers to investigate and usually require the memorialist to join them.

sentences.zh: 光鼐既將坐譴，卒得自白，阿桂之賢也。

translations.literal: Guangnai was about to incur censure, yet finally obtained self-vindication—the worthiness of Agui.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Guangnai nearly faced punishment but was finally cleared—credit Agui's integrity.

sentences.zh: 灃劾國泰發庫藏掩覆，論者謂劉墉密與灃商榷，蓋亦有力焉。

translations.literal: Feng impeached Guotai and exposed treasury cover-ups; commentators say Liu Yong secretly consulted with Feng—the influence was likely there too.
translations.idiomatic: Feng's exposure of Guotai's treasury fraud owed something, commentators say, to Liu Yong's quiet backing.

sentences.zh: 漱芳、錫寶、壯圖皆不能實其言，大臣怙寵亂政，民迫於飢寒，卒成禍亂。

translations.literal: Shufang, Xibao, and Zhuangtu all could not substantiate their words; ministers clung to favor and disrupted government; the people were pressed by hunger and cold—finally forming calamity and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shufang, Cao Xibao, and Yin Zhuangtu could not prove their charges; favored ministers corrupted government while the people suffered hunger and cold, bringing ruin in the end.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，古昔聖王兢兢，重畏民碞，良有以也！

translations.literal: Alas! Ancient sage kings were vigilant and fearful, heavily revering the anger of the people—truly there was reason for it!
translations.idiomatic: Alas—the caution of ancient sage-kings toward popular anger was well founded indeed!
